A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NoisyRollout study. Their main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison, including material moved between sections.

before.justification: v2 reports original RL training and benchmark results, augmentation ablations, perception comparisons, and gradient analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains those original empirical results and additionally reports benchmark performance using rotation augmentation.

M1.justification: v4 adds rotation with image expansion as a successful augmentation variant alongside Gaussian noise; v2 reports rotation among unsuccessful alternatives. This is a limited adaptation of the image transformation. Hybrid rollout grouping, clean-input policy updates, the GRPO objective, and noise annealing remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions train on Geometry3K and MMK12 and evaluate on Geometry3K, MathVerse, MathVision, MathVista, WeMath, and HallusionBench. The rotation experiment retains this coverage. DMControl and ProcGen appear only in v4's related-work discussion.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 and the matched existing ablations retain their comparison methods. The added rotation variant uses the existing GRPO baseline. Newly discussed methods such as RAD, CURL, and DrQ are not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: The reported optimization budget for the 32B model on MMK12 changes from 84 steps in v2 Table 12 to 70 in v4 Table 13. v4 also reports an additional rotation-with-expansion experiment. The budget revision does not establish that the retained benchmark experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 Table 5 extends augmentation sensitivity analysis with successful rotation results. Appendix A retains the failed rotation/cropping curves but identifies the rotation as lacking expansion, and removes the unsuccessful randomized-augmentation account. Other ablations, gradient analyses, and case studies remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same four data-sampling seeds, five-run gradient-update averaging, and gradient uncertainty display. v4's checklist explicitly acknowledges missing main-result error bars but introduces no new uncertainty estimates, run counts, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: New v4 Table 5 reports rotation scores of 52.5, 28.1, 71.9, 68.1, and 70.2 across the five benchmarks, averaging 58.2 versus GRPO's 57.2 and Gaussian noise's 59.2. Existing benchmark values remain unchanged. The qualitative finding about unsuccessful randomized augmentation is omitted.

T1.justification: Equations 1–3, advantage calculations, and the gradient-contribution definitions remain equivalent. Algorithm 1 is relocated without changing its mathematical content. Neither version supplies formal convergence proofs.

C1.justification: v4's abstract explicitly extends the effectiveness claim across augmentation types, naming Gaussian noise and rotation. Claims about benchmark performance, sample efficiency, model/data scaling, and no additional training cost are retained.

C2.justification: v2 emphasizes unsuccessful rotation/cropping and Gaussian noise's regularizing role. v4 distinguishes successful rotation with expansion from information-destroying rotation without expansion, sharpening the condition that augmentations preserve essential visual content. The dedicated limitations discussion is unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 specifies expand=True for successful rotation, adds asset licenses in Appendix K, and discloses LLM-assisted data processing/filtering in the checklist. Its hyperparameter table revises the 32B MMK12 step count. The code and model/data collection links are unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds a substantive subsection on data augmentation in visual RL, covering RAD, CURL, DrQ/DrQ-v2, DrAC, SVEA, SPR, and domain randomization. This supplies a previously missing, directly relevant research lineage and distinguishes visual control from multimodal reasoning, substantially expanding the paper's positioning.

P1.justification: v4 condenses the abstract, removes the introduction's contribution bullets, rewrites the augmentation discussion, and moves Algorithm 1 into the method section. It adds acknowledgements, a conference checklist, and licenses. Most scientific prose and the main section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds the augmentation comparison table, moves the workflow figure to the first page and Algorithm 1 into the main text, and rearranges existing displays. Figure 9 receives a more specific caption while retaining its curves. Existing plots and table structures are largely preserved.

improvement.justification: The rotation results and expansion distinction strengthen the evidence for augmentation generality and clarify failure conditions. The new visual-RL related-work subsection substantially improves context, while license disclosure and the relocated algorithm improve usability. These support a limited overall improvement: headline results remain unchanged, rotation settings are only partly specified, and the 84-to-70-step budget revision is unexplained.
